strategy: none — selection methodology tested on CFTC positioning

method.cftc_source: CFTC disaggregated futures-only history, downloaded 2026-08-24; 503 gold weeks, 2017-01-03 to 2026-08-18

windows.mon_tue_ret: Friday close to next Tuesday close — the post-publication window
windows.tue_only_ret: Monday close to Tuesday close — what a Monday-close condition can use

limitations: 274 weeks joined to a daily series starting 2021-05. The CFTC history reaches 2017 and 503 weeks; the binding constraint is now price data, not positioning.
Returns are measured on daily closes. The intraday shape of the sweep hypothesis — break the low, then recover within the session — needs 30-minute data, which covers only 137 of these weeks.

The consensus votes were chosen by the researcher, not optimised, and no record shows the five-vote cutoff was fixed before the by-vote table was seen. A search over vote definitions would find better ones and would need its own correction.
32 weeks have no separate Monday bar and Tuesday bar (for example a US Monday holiday). They are excluded from the Tuesday-only comparisons and kept in the Friday-to-Tuesday ones.
The claim-2 cutoffs (quantiles and medians) are computed inside each half, so the second half is not a strict out-of-sample test of first-half cutoffs.
No result changes formal S1 or S2 logic, live risk, or an entry checklist.

claim_1_monday_sweep.claim: Monday after the release breaks the low, sweeps liquidity, then rises.

circular_version.note: Conditions on whether Monday broke Friday's low, then measures a return that includes Monday. The break is not knowable until Monday is over, so this asks whether a down Monday was down.

clean_version.note: Same condition, evaluated at Monday's close, measuring Tuesday alone. Condition strictly precedes the window it predicts. Weeks without a separate Monday bar and Tuesday bar (same_bar) are excluded: their Tuesday-only return is 0 by construction.

including_same_bar_weeks.note: Earlier computation, kept for comparison: same-bar weeks counted as 0% (a loss).

sweep_and_recover.note: The claimed shape: broke the low AND closed up — a real sweep. Same-bar weeks excluded, as in the clean version.

claim_1_monday_sweep.reading: The circular version shows a win-rate gap of -30.06 points between weeks that broke Friday's low and weeks that did not. That gap comes from measuring a window that contains the condition. Evaluated at Monday's close and measuring Tuesday alone, the gap is +1.80 points.

claim_2_fifty_percent_rule.claim: A condition with a win rate above 50% is alpha.
claim_2_fifty_percent_rule.note: Conditions that select exactly the same weeks in both halves are counted once. The quantile and median cutoffs inside each condition are computed within each half (the second half uses its own cutoffs, not the first half's), so the second half is not a strict out-of-sample test of first-half cutoffs.
claim_2_fifty_percent_rule.reading: The baseline moved 8.75 points between halves, so the same 50% threshold means 'beats the market' in one period and 'loses to it' in the other. A condition's win rate ranks it against the period, not against chance, and the period-to-period correlation of that rank is -0.143.

claim_3_consensus.claim: Several conditions agreeing at once is alpha.

five_or_more_walk_forward.note: Medians from prior weeks only; no lookahead of any kind.
five_or_more_walk_forward.caveat: n=19. The walk-forward selection looks better than the full-sample one on both measures, which is the opposite of the usual direction and a reason to treat it as thin rather than as confirmation.

opportunity_cost.note: What trading only the consensus weeks would have captured.

claim_3_consensus.reading: In sample, five or more votes gives a win-rate gap of +13.74 points (permutation p 0.1883, not separable from chance at 0.05) and a mean weekly return gap of -0.1298 points (permutation p 0.6497, not separable from chance at 0.05). Walk-forward (n=19): win-rate gap +13.83 (p 0.3393, not separable from chance at 0.05), mean return gap +0.1570 (p 0.678, not separable from chance at 0.05). Win rate and expectancy are different quantities; the gaps are described here, and a gap marked not separable is not evidence of either a gain or a loss.
